scope.description: Subtests: three-voter control, three-voter injected_store_error, injected_store_error_then_restart, control_five_voters and injected_store_error_five_voters (one or two escalation steps), and the new injected_store_error_then_snapshot. The snapshot subtest builds the same three-voter cluster with the fault wrapper, configures SnapshotThreshold 1, TrailingLogs 0 and a one-hour SnapshotInterval, runs the same partition/divergence/higher-term replacement history with the injected StoreLogs error, confirms the wedge, removes the fault, has the leader take a snapshot, applies one client entry, and then samples the wedged node's certificate, store first/last index, commit index and store counters every 200 ms for four seconds, together with the leader's probe, the store's first index before and after the snapshot and the snapshot future's error.
assumptions: With TrailingLogs 0 the leader compacts its log up to the snapshot index, so its replication to a peer whose next index is pinned at the beginning can no longer read the entries and must send a snapshot, which is the library's own ErrLogNotFound to SEND_SNAP path.
The snapshot is triggered through the public Snapshot API on a leader whose FSM has applied state (MockFSM), so the snapshot content is the applied state at that moment.
The new client entry produced after the snapshot is what shows whether replication resumes past the install rather than only that the installed state is consistent.

A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface; the wrapper returns it without touching the underlying store, and the fault is not re-armed during the snapshot phase.
excluded: No production code is modified; compaction is configured through Config and snapshots are taken through the public API.
No restart is performed in this subtest; the restart path is covered by its own receipt.

basis.prefix: The snapshot subtest prints truncation_before_heal, truncation_after_heal and truncation_after_disarm like the other cases, then truncation_after_snapshot with snapshot_error, store_first_before, store_first_after, cert_samples, store_last_samples, store_first_samples, commit_samples (200 ms interval over four seconds), the wedged and leader probes, and elapsed_ms.

before.description: Five subtests share one harness: control and injected_store_error on three voters with one escalation step, injected_store_error_then_restart on three voters, and control_five_voters and injected_store_error_five_voters on five voters with two escalation steps. Each case builds the cluster from the library's own in-memory components with a legal fault-injecting LogStore wrapper on the node that becomes the initial leader, runs the partition/divergence/higher-term-replacement history, heals, samples the certificate and store for 1500 ms, removes the fault and samples once more, then removes one healthy voter per step (disconnecting it in both directions) and applies one client entry per step while recording the leader's commit index over 1500 ms, whether that apply future completes, its error, and the leader's and the wedged node's probes with every node's state and term.
assumptions: Removing a healthy voter at the transport level models that voter failing; the remaining voters keep their membership in the configuration, so the quorum size stays the configuration's quorum.
The wedged replica stays connected in every step, because it must keep receiving the leader's retries for the margin claim to be about the wedge rather than about an unreachable node.
A LogStore returning an error from StoreLogs is an allowed outcome of the interface, and the wrapper returns it without touching the underlying store.
The control and faulted five-voter cases differ only in whether that one StoreLogs call returned an error.
excluded: No production code is modified and no fault other than the single store error is injected.
No restart, snapshot install or leader-side compaction is exercised in this experiment; the restart path is covered by the earlier receipt.

prefix.before: Each subtest prints the CA_EVENT lines described before; peer_loss_after_wedge now carries mode, step, voters (the configuration size), removed_voter, leader, leader_state, leader_term, commit_before, commit_samples over 1500 ms, apply_future_done, apply_future_error, leader_probe, wedged_node_probe and state_and_term.

revision_reason: Same investigation and staging, extended with a subtest that repairs the wedged node through the snapshot route instead of a restart: aggressive compaction settings, a leader-triggered snapshot after the wedge, and a new entry produced afterwards so the observation covers replication resuming and not just state consistency.
